features.name: New game and basic board initialization
steps: Show the unrevealed board, remaining-mine count, timer, and center emoji
Tap any cell for the first time to start the game
features.expected: The Easy screenshot is explicitly 9×9 with 10 mines; the timer should be 00:00 before starting; after the board is generated the mine positions, numbers, and blank cells must be mutually consistent; timing starts after the first valid action

features.name: Single-cell reveal and number generation
steps: If there are surrounding mines a number 1–8 is shown
Tap different positions repeatedly to verify the numbers
features.expected: The number must equal the total mines in at most 8 neighboring cells; numbers must not be displayed randomly; the screenshot shows that numbers such as 1, 2, and 3 have different colors

features.name: Chain expansion in the blank region
steps: Tap a blank cell with no surrounding mines
Also expand the numbered cells on the boundaries of these regions
features.expected: One of Minesweeper's most core pieces of business logic; requires Flood Fill/BFS/DFS-style chain expansion; it stops spreading at numbered boundary cells and must not pass through mines or flags

features.name: Flag and unflag cells
steps: Perform the marking operation on an unrevealed suspicious cell
Operate again to cancel the flag
features.expected: Flags may only be used on unrevealed cells; a flagged cell must not be revealed normally; flagging/unflagging must maintain the global remaining-mine count; the winning board in the screenshot shows several orange flags

features.name: Correctly complete a game
steps: Gradually reveal safe cells and mark mines according to the number logic
features.expected: The win condition should be based on all safe cells being revealed rather than simply the number of flags equalling the number of mines; after winning the center emoji switches to 😎, a green "You Win!" banner appears, the timer freezes, and the board keeps its final state

features.name: Mine hit and failure state
steps: Show the exploded cell and the other mine positions
features.expected: After hitting a mine the current cell shows an obvious explosion and the other mines show bombs; the center emoji changes to the failure state; a red Game Over banner appears; the timer stops and no further normal revealing is possible

features.name: In-game state feedback and restarting
steps: Observe the mine count, timer, and emoji
Tap the emoji button in the top center to restart
The new board returns to the initial state
features.expected: The emoji carries the game state and the Restart entry; after restarting the timer, cells, flags, remaining-mine count, and win/lose state must be reset; no data from the previous game may remain

features.name: Easy preset difficulty
steps: Select Easy again to start another game
features.expected: The screenshot explicitly shows Easy as 9×9 / 10 mines; mine layouts must be regenerated for different new games; the difficulty button's selected state must change correctly

features.name: Medium / Hard preset difficulty switching
steps: Verify the board size and parameter changes
features.expected: The three presets must not merely change the title; the board size, mine density, or rule parameters must switch with the difficulty; switching difficulty should start the corresponding new game and reset the game state

features.name: Core rule consistency across difficulties
steps: Perform reveal, flag, blank expansion, mine-hit, and win operations on Easy, Medium, and Hard respectively
features.expected: Regardless of board size, the adjacent-mine counts, chain expansion, flags, and win/lose logic must be consistent; a large board must not have out-of-bounds errors or neighbor-count mistakes

features.name: Custom custom board
features.expected: The screenshot explicitly supports custom Grid size and Mines; the example is 20×20 with 40 mines (10%); the generated board's actual cell count and mine count must match the configuration

features.name: Custom parameter linkage and boundary constraints
steps: Gradually change the board size in Custom
features.expected: The mine count and percentage must link correctly; illegal configurations such as mines ≥ total cells must be avoided; the slider, the numeric display, and the final generated result must be consistent

features.name: Safe first tap
steps: Click a different cell for the first tap in each game
Verify that the first tap does not immediately hit a mine
features.expected: This is excellent benchmark state logic. It must not merely show a switch in the UI; when generating/adjusting the minefield the first clicked cell must be safe while the rest of the board keeps the configured mine count

features.name: Behavior with Safe first tap disabled
steps: The first tap is no longer force-protected
features.expected: After the toggle is disabled the first-tap protection must not continue to be applied secretly; normal random mine placement logic must still be satisfied

features.name: Fog of War custom rules
steps: Compare the display/information visibility between normal mode and Fog mode
features.expected: Focus on verifying that the rule toggles genuinely affect the board display and interaction state; merely persisting a boolean is not enough. The specific visual presentation is reproduced per the target app's actual observable results

features.name: Custom combination configuration
steps: Adjust to a higher/lower mine density
Combine Fog of War with Safe first tap
features.expected: A multi-parameter state combination; board generation, first-tap protection, Fog display, adjacent-mine counting, and the win/lose conditions must all work together without inconsistency from the stacked rules

features.name: Random minefield generation correctness
steps: Restart several games in a row with the same difficulty
Randomly spot-check several numbered cells against the actual surrounding mines in each game
features.expected: Each game should generate a new valid layout; the total mine count is fixed; the numbers must be computed from that game's actual mine positions rather than using a pre-made visual template

features.name: Boundary / corner adjacent-mine computation
steps: Construct or randomly find corner, edge, and interior cells
Check against the surrounding mine count
features.expected: A corner has at most 3 neighbors, an edge at most 5, and the interior at most 8; this is excellent for detecting array-out-of-bounds and neighbor-enumeration errors in the reproduction

features.name: Flag and reveal conflict state
features.expected: Test the same cell's state machine: Hidden → Flagged → Hidden → Revealed; it must not be Flagged and Revealed at the same time

features.name: Win/lose state locking
steps: Then tap the board; lose a game
Verify separately that the game no longer changes logically
features.expected: Both Win and Lose are terminal states; the timer should freeze; after Game Over the user must not continue flagging or revealing to cause a second win

features.name: Large-board performance and interaction
steps: Custom select 20×20 / 40 mines or a larger configuration
features.expected: Test the reproduction app's rendering and state updates with hundreds of cells; Flood Fill, adjacent-mine counting, and global win/lose detection should not noticeably lag or be missed

features.name: Complete comprehensive gameplay flow
features.expected: Best used as a comprehensive E2E: verify board generation, number computation, Flood Fill, flags, timing, mine count, Lose, Restart, Win, difficulty switching, custom parameters, and state reset in one pass
